newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices quiet ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices quiet ahead of data.

text.p: Major U.S. index options trading remained subdued Monday as investors prepared for the week's onslaught of economic news, highlighted by the April employment report due Friday, traders said.
"I think it's more just fear than anything," one broker in Chicago said. "I don't think people want to do anything."
He said a few of his clients had traded some S&P 100 index options, betting on a downward move.
"Maybe they figure the market will sell off into the numbers," he said. "But the market's not cooperating right now."
In late trading, the OEX was up 5.70 at 753.82. The S&P 500 index was up 5.48 at 770.85. June S&P 500 futures were up 5.80 at 774.70.
Fair value for June S&Ps was pegged at roughly 3.55 points over cash, with arbitrage buy programs expected at 4.40 points over and sell programs at about 2.80 points over.

The economic data due this week include the first quarter employment cost index on Tuesday, Chicago purchasing managers index for April on Wedenesday, March personal income and consumption on Thursday and the April jobs report on Friday.
Moby Waller at Investment Research Institute said in a report that investor fear remains high, suggesting the market could be poised for a move higher.
Waller cited the 0.59 reading on the 10-day moving average of the CBOE's equity put/call ratio and the fact that last Thursday's reading was the highest since 1990 as two signs of investor fear.
"Stated simply, this means that speculators are more willing to buy puts versus calls now than they were in the 1996 summer market correction or in the 1994 'stealth' bear market," Waller said.
Waller added that the pricing on certain OEX options suggested investors were willing to pay up for far out-of-the-money puts, another indication the market is not near a top.
Jerry Hegarty at Thomson Financial Services said Thursday and Friday of this week could be positive from first-of-the-month money flows.
"On the other hand, Friday is the monthly employment report which almost always is a major catalyst for volatility," he said in a report.

The broker in Chicago agreed that even if trading volume remains thin for most of the week, volatilities will likely hold firm as investors price-in the chance of a sharp market reaction to the economic data.
With the market moving higher Monday, the CBOE's volatility index, priced off certain OEX options, fell 0.63, or about 2.75 percent, to 22.10. It rose intraday to 23.19 before easing.
